    • What each tool does
      • tools/summarize/ —— AI Chat Daily/Weekly/Monthly Reports
      • tools/research/ —— Paper Discovery and Researcher Analysis
      • tools/benchmark/ —— Performance Benchmarking SuiteCross-platform CPU/GPU FLOPS benchmarking tool, providing unified floating-point performance measurement across different hardware vendors and precision levels. Supports actual GPU execution for NVIDIA(CUDA), Apple Silicon(MPS), and Intel(XPU) (OpenCL may only appear in --info detection), covering precisions such as FP64 / FP32 / FP16 / BF16 / FP8(experimental). Measurement employs warm-up + formal measurement + statistical analysis (median, IQR outlier removal), and explicit GPU synchronization to ensure timing accuracy. Results are accumulated in CSV in append mode (never overwritten, naturally supporting multi-hardware cumulative leaderboards), and can generate interactive HTML reports and leaderboards with Plotly charts, supporting deployment to Hugo websites and submission to public leaderboards.
      • tools/website/ —— Hugo Blog
      • tools/translator/ —— Gradio Document Translator

The gadget README.md (20,768 characters) handed verbatim to 22 models, asking for a project summary and then a usage tutorial in Chinese. Grouped by the tool that called them.

下面是开源项目 gadget 的 README。请你完成两件事：
1. 先用中文总结这个项目：它是什么、仓库结构、每个工具分别做什么。
2. 然后写一份详细的中文使用教程，面向第一次接触这个项目的人，覆盖环境准备、安装、配置，以及每个工具的典型用法（给出可以直接复制的命令）。
只依据 README 里写到的内容，不要编造 README 中没有出现的命令或参数。

===== README.md =====
<README.md 全文，20 768 字符>

Summarize the project in Chinese, then write a detailed Chinese tutorial for a first-time user with copy-pasteable commands. Use only what the README says; do not invent commands or flags.

Conditions: one run per model, no system prompt — read the numbers as orders of magnitude. Cloud models ran serially through their agent CLIs (codex exec / claude -p / cursor-agent --print) in an empty directory, prompt on stdin, so time includes CLI startup. Local models ran cold on an RTX 5090 and their speed is pure decode, so the two speeds are not comparable. Fable 5.1 had --effort high pinned; the other Claude models used the default effort.

Metrics (all regex): “Commands” counts code-block lines starting with pip, python, cd, bash and similar; “Not in README” counts those that, comments stripped and whitespace collapsed, cannot be found in the README; “Facts” is how many of 16 word-for-word README facts the output mentions, and “Missed” lists the rest.

Part One: Project Summary

What are Gadgets

Gadgets (repository directory named gadget/) is a set of daily development tools covering five types of needs: AI conversation summarization, paper research, performance benchmarking, blog publishing, and document translation.

The five tools under tools/ can be used independently. They share the common/ package in the repository root, which provides capabilities such as LLM calls, caching, file writing, translation, and Hugo deployment.

The development workflow and Claude Code skills are located in another repository, ai-companion, at the sibling directory ../ai-companion/, integrated via this repository’s hooks.

Repository Structure

gadget/
├── tools/
│   ├── summarize/      # AI 对话日报、周报、月报
│   ├── research/       # 论文发现、研究者分析、引用图分析
│   ├── benchmark/      # CPU/GPU 性能测试
│   ├── website/        # Hugo 博客、媒体压缩、构建和发布
│   └── translator/     # Gradio 文档翻译器
├── common/             # 工具共用的基础能力
├── scripts/            # 同步、机器配置、检查等维护脚本
├── docs/               # 设计文档、计划、审计报告、历史归档
├── outputs/            # 可重新生成的输出，已被 Git 忽略
├── AGENTS.md           # AI agent 工作协议
├── CLAUDE.md           # Claude Code 仓库指南
└── pyproject.toml      # Python 打包与安装配置

Enter tools/<工具名>/ when modifying tool logic; enter common/ when modifying common capabilities; check scripts/sync.py when modifying synchronization logic; enter the independent ai-companion repository when modifying development workflows or skills.

What the five tools do respectively

Tool Main Function Key Features
Summarize Generates daily, weekly, and monthly reports from AI conversations Supports Claude Code, Codex, Cursor Agent, ChatGPT, and general JSON; supports merging after multi-device export; statistics for token usage and costs
Research Discovers papers, analyzes papers and researchers, analyzes citation relationships Searches sources like arXiv, bioRxiv, PubMed, etc.; provides three-stage LLM evaluation, full paper analysis, OpenReview comment analysis, and researcher profiling
Benchmark Measures CPU/GPU floating-point performance Actual GPU testing supports CUDA, Apple MPS, Intel XPU; covers multiple precisions; results appended to CSV, can generate interactive HTML reports
Website Builds and publishes Hugo blogs Uses PaperMod theme; incremental compression of images and videos; bilingual translation via local models; pushes to GitHub Pages after build
Translator Translates text and files in the browser Based on Gradio; supports .md, .txt, .pdf, .docx and images; protects content like code blocks, URLs, Hugo shortcodes in Markdown

common/ also includes JSON parsing and repair, SHA-256 disk caching with namespaces and TTL, atomic writes, and content hashing. scripts/ is responsible for operations; ai-companion is responsible for code change tracking, testing and HTML reports, as well as development processes like /idea → /ccplan → /ccedit.

Part Two: Beginner Usage TutorialAll commands below are from the provided README. Unless it is a Benchmark or explicitly contains cd, commands are executed in the root directory of the gadget/ repository by default.

The README is positioned as an overview and does not provide complete installation and configuration steps. Missing content will be explicitly stated; no speculative commands will be added.

1. Prepare Environment

The required basic environment is as follows:

Environment or Component Requirements in README
Python 3.10 or newer
Conda Using an environment named AI is recommended, but no creation command is provided
Node.js 18 or newer, only required for the standalone ai-companion repository
Tool Dependencies See requirements.txt in the corresponding directory
rclone Requires configuration first for cross-device synchronization
Hugo Used for website building and local preview
pngquant, HandBrakeCLI Used for website image and video compression
Local Inference Backend Ollama, vLLM, transformers, or GGUF/llamacpp; specific choices are detailed below

If you already have a AI Conda environment, you can execute:

conda activate AI

The README does not provide the clone address for the gadget repository, nor does it provide installation commands for Python, Conda, Ollama, Hugo, rclone, pngquant, or HandBrakeCLI; therefore, a complete “from scratch” installation process cannot be provided here.

2. Install Python Packages and Tool Dependencies

Install common base packages:

pip install -e .

Install common and the extras for Summarize, Research, Benchmark, and Website:

pip install -e ".[all]"

Note: all does not include Translator. If a translator is needed, install it separately:

pip install -e ".[translator]"

If you only need the dependencies corresponding to Website, the README also provides:

pip install -e ".[website]"

Among them, Website extras include torch and transformers used for translation; Translator extras include Gradio and the GGUF translation stack.

3. Prepare Configuration

In the repository root, copy config.example.json to config.json, then modify as needed. The README does not show the complete structure of configuration fields, so configuration content should not be fabricated.

Relevant configuration entry points are as follows:

Configuration Entry Purpose
Root directory config.json Tool settings
sync section of config.json Data synchronization settings
summarize section of config.json Persistent settings related to local Ollama for Summarize
GADGET_CONFIG Override configuration file path
GADGET_LLM_BACKEND Global selection of LLM backend
GADGET_TRANSLATION_BACKEND Select local translation backend
GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL Override translation model
tokens/ API keys and machine initialization configuration table

config.json and tokens/ are ignored by Git; do not commit the contents of tokens/. The README does not provide API key filenames, formats, or assignment examples for the above environment variables.

LLM functionality for Summarize and Research supports selection via --api:

Value Meaning
ollama Default, local Ollama, no API key required; README describes using Gemma4-26B
claude_cli Reuse Claude Code CLI login status, no API key required
anthropic Anthropic API
openai OpenAI API

The README does not provide the complete configuration process for these backends, nor does it show complete command examples with --api.

Translation functionality uses local inference. Special attention should be paid to the fact that the README’s descriptions of the default translation model vary:

  • The Website and Translator sections describe tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B, which is automatically downloaded upon first use; Translator also lists its GGUF variants.
  • Environment Requirements and Notes describe Ollama defaulting to gemma4:26b, while other in-process backends use tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B.

Therefore, based solely on this README, one cannot assert that all translation paths default to the same model.

4. Optional: Machine Initialization and Basic Checks

If you wish to configure a new machine, the README provides two paths:

  • Repository-level Initialization: Fill in tokens/onboard.yaml and run scripts/onboard.py. It will configure SSH, Claude/Codex installation and authentication, pip extras, ai-companion, tool settings, and rclone bootstrap. The README does not provide the complete execution command or YAML examples.
  • Ubuntu Server-level Initialization: The script is located in the ai-companion repository and supports Ubuntu 22.04/24.04. You can check its help first:
bash ../ai-companion/scripts/onboard-server.sh --help

The --companion-repo of the server script should point to the ai-companion repository git@github.com:TzJ2006/ai-companion.git; after splitting, --companion-ref is no longer required. The README does not provide the complete installation command.

After installation, you can run a read-only smoke test:

bash scripts/smoke.sh

It checks the --help, --info, and imports of each tool, without calling LLMs, accessing the network, or writing files.

5. Summarize: Generate AI Conversation Reports

The typical workflow is: export conversation logs from each device → sync via cloud drive or manual aggregation → merge daily to generate daily reports → generate weekly and monthly reports after daily reports have accumulated.

Phase one, export all dates that have not yet been exported:

python -m summarize daily export

In multi-device scenarios, each device exports separately, then logs are aggregated. Phase two, sync all dates and merge them daily:

python -m summarize daily merge --sync-all

Generate a weekly report for a specified week based on existing daily reports, and deploy:

python -m summarize weekly generate --week 2026-W12 --deploy

Generate a monthly report for a specified month based on existing daily reports, and deploy:

python -m summarize monthly generate --month 2026-02 --deploy

2026-W12 and 2026-02 are example values from the README; replace them with the target week or month when in use.

You can also run the full automated process:

python -m summarize auto --deploy

It performs export, merging, weekly reports, monthly reports, and deployment.

This tool uses the ccusage 20.x source-based namespace command to count tokens and costs for each agent CLI. The README does not provide the installation command for ccusage, conversation source paths, or exported data formats.

The old daily_summary.py, weekly_summary.py, and monthly_summary.py entry points are still compatible, but using the above python -m summarize format is recommended.

6. Research: Discover Papers, Analyze Researchers, and Citation Relationships

Research uses a single entry point tools/research/research_scout.py.

Run a complete paper research workflow for a project:

python tools/research/research_scout.py report --project my-project

It performs searching, three-stage evaluation, and report generation. The three stages are rapid screening, in-depth evaluation, and citation impact analysis.

my-project is an example project name. The README does not explain how projects are defined or provide the project configuration format, so project configuration cannot be completed based solely on this README.

Search using natural language:

python tools/research/research_scout.py ask "找 Pieter Abbeel 最近的机器人操作论文"

This command will automatically select the search source.

Generate researcher profiles:

python tools/research/research_scout.py profile "Sergey Levine"

The profiling feature combines arXiv, Semantic Scholar, and LLM to analyze research trajectories, calculate hierarchical scores, and discover mentor-student relationships through homepage information and co-authorship patterns. It also supports disambiguation of same-name authors and reverse lookup.

Analyze paper citation graphs:

python tools/research/research_scout.py citations 2301.12597

Input supports arXiv ID or DOI; analysis includes forward citations, backward references, and LLM-based impact interpretation.

Deploy research reports to Hugo:

python tools/research/research_scout.py deploy

The README also introduces --insight deep paper analysis: downloading full texts, analyzing writing structure, publication strategies, and reusable knowledge, matching OpenReview comments, and synthesizing cross-paper writing guides. However, it does not provide complete invocation examples, so no speculative commands are concatenated here.

7. Benchmark: Test CPU/GPU Performance

Benchmark commands have special directory requirements: enter tools/benchmark/ first.

cd tools/benchmark

Run all tests:

python -m benchmark.cli

Test CPU only:

python -m benchmark.cli --cpu-only

Test GPU only:

python -m benchmark.cli --gpu-only

Run tests and generate an HTML report:

python -m benchmark.cli --report

Run tests, generate a report, and publish to Hugo via /benchmark/:

python -m benchmark.cli --report --deploy

These are different running methods; choose as needed.

Tests use warm-up, formal measurement, median statistics, and IQR outlier removal, and explicitly synchronize the GPU. Results are saved in an append mode to CSV, facilitating the accumulation of scores across multiple hardware types.

Actual GPU testing supports NVIDIA CUDA, Apple Silicon MPS, and Intel XPU. OpenCL may appear in the detection results of --info, but it is not listed as an actual GPU testing backend in the README. Precision includes FP64, FP32, FP16, BF16, and experimental FP8.

The README mentions a public leaderboard submission feature but does not provide the submission command or specific hardware driver installation steps.

After execution, subsequent tool commands must be run after returning to the gadget/ root directory in the terminal.

8. Website: Preview and Publish Hugo Blog

If Website extras are not yet installed, execute in the root directory:

pip install -e ".[website]"

Local preview:

cd tools/website && hugo server -D

-D indicates including drafts during preview.

macOS/Linux build and publish:

cd tools/website && bash update.sh

Windows execution in the repository root:

powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/website/update.ps1

The Windows script will enter its own directory automatically.

The publish script performs incremental media compression, Hugo building, and pushes to Pages. Incremental compression is based on .last_build: images use pngquant, and videos use HandBrakeCLI.

These two update scripts will publish the website, not just generate a local preview. The corresponding site in the README is https://tzj2006.github.io/, and the deployment repository is tzj2006/tzj2006.github.io; the README does not explain how to change to your own site or configure push authentication.

Automatically generated content is written directly to:

  • tools/website/content
  • tools/website/static

These files carry the gadget_generated tag; handwritten files without this tag will not be overwritten.

tools/website/public/ is an independent deployment repository, which is automatically committed and pushed by the build script; do not commit directly to it.9. Translator: Translate documents in the browser

Install dependencies in the repository root:

pip install -e ".[translator]"

Start the interface:

python -m translator

It will open a Gradio GUI in the browser. You can translate text or .md, .txt, .pdf, .docx, and image files within the interface, and switch models via the model management in the interface.

Language selection behavior:

  • When the source language is set to auto, it detects based on the CJK character ratio of the text.
  • When the target language is set to auto, it switches between Chinese and English.

The translator reuses common.engine.create_engine() to automatically select the backend: if the model tag has been pulled, it automatically prioritizes Ollama; the fallback for Windows is transformers, Linux prioritizes vLLM, and llama-cpp/GGUF options are provided for low VRAM scenarios.

Models reside in memory; models are lazy-loaded on demand when switching. Discrepancies between the default model and environmental requirements are explained in the configuration section. The README does not provide commands for manually pulling models, specifying ports, or translating files via the command line.

outputs/
├── logs/         # 导出日志、运行日志等中间产物

├── cache/        # LLM 缓存、搜索缓存

V. Summarize: Generating Reports from AI Conversations

Supports reading Claude Code, Codex, Cursor Agent, ChatGPT, and general JSON conversation records.

It employs two stages: first exporting on each device, then aggregating and merging to generate daily reports; after accumulating daily reports, weekly and monthly reports can be generated.

Step one: On each device where conversation records need to be collected, export all dates that have not yet been exported:

python -m summarize daily export

Step two: Synchronize aggregated export records via cloud drive or manual copying, then synchronize all dates and merge them day by day:

python -m summarize daily merge --sync-all

Step three: Generate weekly or monthly reports based on existing daily reports. The following uses example dates from the README and includes deployment operations:

python -m summarize weekly generate --week 2026-W12 --deploy

python -m summarize monthly generate --month 2026-02 --deploy

You can also run the full pipeline, executing export, merge, weekly report, monthly report, and deployment in sequence:

python -m summarize auto --deploy

Tips:- --deploy will trigger deployment; relevant website configurations should be prepared before use.

  • Token usage and cost statistics are completed via various source commands in ccusage 20.x.
  • Old daily_summary.py, weekly_summary.py, and monthly_summary.py entries are still compatible, but using the above module entries is recommended.
  • The README does not provide path configurations for various conversation sources, a universal JSON format, or the ccusage installation command.

I. Project Overview#

Gadgets is a collection of daily development tools covering AI conversation summarization, paper retrieval, performance testing, blog publishing, and document translation. The five tools under tools/ can be used separately; they share the common/ package in the repository root.

Location Role
tools/summarize/ Summarizes conversations from Claude Code, Codex, Cursor Agent, ChatGPT, etc., generates daily, weekly, and monthly reports, and statistics usage and costs
tools/research/ Retrieves and evaluates papers, analyzes researchers, analyzes citation relationships, and generates research reports
tools/benchmark/ Measures CPU and GPU floating-point performance, accumulates CSV results, and generates interactive HTML reports
tools/website/ Hugo blog; handles media compression, content translation, building, and publishing
tools/translator/ Local document translation page based on Gradio, supporting text and various file formats
common/ Shared LLM calling, caching, file writing, translation, and Hugo publishing capabilities for all tools
scripts/ Operations scripts such as data synchronization, new machine configuration, and smoke checks
docs/ Design documents, plans, and historical materials
outputs/ Generated logs, reports, caches, data, images, and backups; ignored by Git

ai-companion is an independent repository located in ../ai-companion/, providing development workflows and skills, and is not part of the Gadgets tools/. Blog content is written directly to tools/website/content or tools/website/static; the website’s public/ is a separate deployment repository.

8. Common Maintenance Commands and Output Locations#

The entry point for data synchronization scripts, as well as the cross-device push/pull forms provided in the README:

python scripts/sync.py
python scripts/sync.py push/pull

The second line is the README’s combined representation of the two operations; in actual use, choose one from push and pull. Synchronization requires pre-configuring rclone, with settings located in the sync section of config.json.

Perform a cross-tool smoke test that does not call LLMs, access the network, or write files:

bash scripts/smoke.sh

View the environment settings output from the local Ollama service script:

eval "$(bash scripts/serve_local_llm.sh env)"

Generated artifacts are concentrated in outputs/: logs/ for intermediate logs, reports/ for final reports, cache/ for cache, data/ for structured data, images/ for charts and images, and backups/ for backups of overwrite operations. This directory is ignored by Git. For more detailed configuration values, data formats, and troubleshooting, the README explicitly points to the repository’s TUTORIAL.md and each tool’s own documentation; this tutorial does not fabricate those unshown steps.

This tool reads conversation records from Claude Code, Codex, Cursor Agent, ChatGPT, or general JSON formats to generate daily, weekly, and monthly reports via LLM. In multi-device scenarios, first export records on the devices, then synchronize or manually aggregate them, and finally merge them by date to generate reports.

I. Project Summary#

1. What is Gadget#

Gadget is a set of practical tools accumulated from daily development, mainly covering five types of tasks:

  • Generation of daily, weekly, and monthly reports for AI conversation logs
  • Academic paper discovery, deep paper analysis, and researcher profiling
  • CPU/GPU floating-point performance testing
  • Hugo blog building, translation, media compression, and automatic publishing
  • Local document translation

The five tools under tools/ are independent of each other and can be used separately. They collectively depend on the common/ package in the repository root. common/ provides general capabilities such as LLM invocation, JSON repair, disk caching, atomic writing, local translation, and Hugo deployment.

The project’s development workflow and Claude Code skills are not in this repository, but in an adjacent independent repository ../ai-companion/, integrated into Gadget through hooks under .claude/ and .codex/.

The project uses the GPL-3 license.

2. Repository Structure#

gadget/
├── tools/
│   ├── summarize/      # AI 对话日报、周报、月报
│   ├── research/       # 论文发现、研究者分析、引用图谱
│   ├── benchmark/      # CPU/GPU 性能测试
│   ├── website/        # Hugo 博客构建和发布
│   └── translator/     # Gradio 文档翻译器
├── common/             # 所有工具共享的基础设施
├── scripts/            # 同步、初始化、维护脚本
├── docs/               # 设计文档、ECL 计划、审计和历史文档
├── outputs/            # 自动生成的输出，已被 gitignore
├── AGENTS.md           # AI agent 工作协议
├── CLAUDE.md           # Claude Code 仓库指南
└── pyproject.toml      # Python 包及 extras 配置

When modifying different types of functions, the corresponding locations are as follows:

Target Location
Modify a specific tool tools/<tool>/
Modify common capabilities like LLM, cache, translation, Hugo deployment, etc. common/
Modify data synchronization scripts/sync.py
One-time configuration for new machines scripts/onboard.py
Modify development workflow or skill ../ai-companion/
View design and execution plans docs/、docs/ecl/

3. What Each Tool Does#

Summarize#

Reads AI conversation logs from Claude Code, Codex, Cursor Agent, ChatGPT, or general JSON formats to generate structured daily, weekly, and monthly reports.

It adopts a multi-device, two-stage process:

  1. Export conversation logs on each device.
  2. Aggregate them via cloud drive synchronization or manual copying, then generate reports on a daily basis.

Once daily reports accumulate to a certain amount, weekly and monthly trend summaries can be further generated.

It uses the ccusage 20.x source-based command to statistics token usage and costs for different agent CLIs, such as ccusage claude、ccusage codex、ccusage gemini.

It supports four LLM backends:

  • ollama: Default, runs locally, no API key required
  • claude_cli: Reuses Claude Code CLI login status, no API key required
  • anthropic
  • openai

Research#

A unified academic research tool, with the entry point:

tools/research/research_scout.py

It has four main capabilities:

  • Paper Discovery: Searches for papers from arXiv, bioRxiv, and PubMed; generates research weekly reports through a three-stage LLM process (“Quick Screening → Deep Evaluation → Citation Impact”), and can publish to Hugo.
  • Deep Paper Insights: Downloads full paper texts, analyzes writing structure, publication strategies, and reusable knowledge; matches OpenReview comments to analyze reviewer consensus and controversies; finally synthesizes cross-paper writing guides.
  • Researcher Profiling: Retrieves paper and citation data from ArXiv and Semantic Scholar to generate research trajectory analysis and layered scoring, and infers mentor-student relationships through personal homepages and co-authorship patterns.
  • Citation Graph: Utilizes the Semantic Scholar API to analyze forward citations and backward references, then uses an LLM to interpret paper impact.

It also supports four LLM backends: ollama、claude_cli、anthropic and openai.

Benchmark#

A cross-platform CPU/GPU FLOPS floating-point performance testing tool, supporting:

  • NVIDIA CUDA
  • Apple Silicon MPS
  • Intel XPU

OpenCL may appear in --info detection results, but the README does not state that it can perform actual GPU tests.

Supported precisions include:

  • FP64
  • FP32
  • FP16
  • BF16
  • FP8, experimental support

The testing process includes warmup, formal measurement, median statistics, IQR outlier removal, and explicit GPU synchronization.

Results are written to CSV in an append mode and will not overwrite existing results, allowing for the accumulation of data from multiple hardware units to form leaderboards. The tool can also use Plotly to generate interactive HTML reports and publish them to the Hugo website or submit them to public leaderboards.

Website#

A Hugo static blog named “TzJ’s Net”, using the PaperMod theme, with the target site being https://tzj2006.github.io/.

Main capabilities include:

  • Only compressing media files that have changed after .last_build
  • Compressing images using pngquant
  • Compressing videos using HandBrakeCLI
  • Generating bilingual content using local models
  • Automatically building the Hugo website
  • Automatically committing and pushing the GitHub Pages deployment repository

Daily, weekly, and monthly reports, research reports, benchmark pages, and images are written directly by the deployment process:

tools/website/content
tools/website/static

Automatically generated files carry the gadget_generated tag. Hand-written files without this tag will not be overwritten.

tools/website/public/ is an independent deployment repository corresponding to tzj2006/tzj2006.github.io, and files should not be manually committed to it.

Translator#

A Gradio-based local document translation web application with an interface similar to Google Translate.

Supports translating:

  • Plain text
  • .md
  • .txt
  • .pdf
  • .docx
  • Images

It attempts to preserve Markdown formatting and protects snippets like code blocks, URLs, and Hugo shortcodes.

Translation is performed entirely via local inference without using cloud LLM APIs. It automatically selects the backend via common.engine.create_engine():

  • Prioritizes Ollama if the corresponding model has been pulled
  • Falls back to transformers on Windows
  • Prioritizes vLLM on Linux
  • Uses llama.cpp/GGUF for low VRAM scenarios

The default model is:

tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B

The GGUF version is:

tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B-GGUF

Models are automatically downloaded upon first use. Once loaded, models remain in memory, with lazy loading applied when switching models as needed.

When the source language is set to auto, it auto-detects based on the proportion of CJK characters in the text; when the target language is set to auto, it automatically switches between Chinese-to-English and English-to-Chinese.

4. Common Modules and Operations Scripts#

common/#

A common Python package providing:

  • A unified two-layer LLM API
  • JSON parsing and repair
  • SHA-256 disk caching with namespaces and TTL
  • Atomic writing and content hashing
  • Local translation engine
  • Bilingual content generation
  • Cross-platform Hugo deployment

scripts/#

Main scripts include:- sync.py: Synchronizes summarize, website, research, benchmark, and backups data via rclone, and also supports generating and deploying DAG sites.

  • onboard.py: One-time initialization for new machines, responsible for SSH, Claude/Codex CLI, authentication, Python extras, AI Companion, tool configuration, and rclone bootstrap.
  • smoke.sh: Read-only smoke test that checks help, hardware information, and imports without calling LLM, network, or performing writes.
  • serve_local_llm.sh: Creates Ollama model variants suitable for summarize and outputs environment variables.
  • language.py: Hugo bilingual content audit and summarize report renaming.
  • profile_translation.py: Translation engine GPU profiler.

AI Companion#

../ai-companion/ is a standalone Node.js/TypeScript repository providing:

  • Function-level code change logs
  • Test and HTML report generation
  • /idea → /ccplan → /ccedit planning and execution workflow
  • Claude Code and Codex integration
  • Skills such as optimization, debugging, auditing, cleaning, paper writing, etc.

Node.js 18+ is only required when using this standalone repository.

Project Overview#

Gadgets is a collection of daily tools for developers, covering five categories of tasks:

  • Generation of daily, weekly, and monthly reports from AI conversation logs
  • Academic paper retrieval, researcher analysis, and citation mapping
  • CPU/GPU performance benchmarking
  • Automated Hugo blog building, media compression, and publishing
  • Local model-driven document translation

Each directory under tools/ is an independently usable tool; the common/ in the root directory provides shared capabilities, such as LLM calls, caching, JSON parsing, atomic writes, translation engines, and Hugo deployment. The development workflow and Claude Code skills are not in this repository, but in the independent repository ../ai-companion/ at the same level.

Repository Structure#

gadget/
├── tools/
│   ├── summarize/   # AI 对话日报 / 周报 / 月报
│   ├── research/    # 论文发现、研究者分析、引用图谱
│   ├── benchmark/   # CPU/GPU 性能测试
│   ├── website/     # Hugo 博客及自动发布
│   └── translator/  # Gradio 文档翻译器
├── common/          # 所有工具共享的基础能力
├── scripts/         # 同步、初始化、检查等运维脚本
├── docs/            # 设计文档、ECL 计划、审计与历史资料
├── outputs/         # 可重新生成的输出文件（已忽略 Git）
├── AGENTS.md        # AI Agent 工作流程协议
├── CLAUDE.md        # Claude Code 仓库说明
└── pyproject.toml   # Python 打包与依赖配置

Generated results are unified in outputs/:

outputs/
├── logs/      # 导出及运行日志
├── reports/   # Markdown、JSON、HTML 报告
├── cache/     # LLM 与搜索缓存
├── data/      # CSV、JSON 等结构化数据
├── images/    # 图表和生成图片
└── backups/   # 强制覆盖时的备份

Hugo website content is written directly to tools/website/content and tools/website/static.

Tool Purposes#

Tool Purpose
summarize Reads conversation logs from Claude Code, Codex, Cursor Agent, ChatGPT, or general JSON to generate daily, weekly, and monthly reports, and statistics for token usage and costs of various Agent CLIs.
research Discovers papers from sources like arXiv, bioRxiv, PubMed, etc.; can perform deep paper insights, researcher profiling, mentor-student relationship inference, and forward/backward citation analysis.
benchmark Tests CPU/GPU floating-point performance across platforms, supporting CUDA, Apple MPS, Intel XPU, and generating HTML charts, leaderboards, and publishing to Hugo.
website A Hugo static blog with capabilities for incremental image/video compression, automatic translation, building, and pushing to GitHub Pages.
translator A Gradio-based local document translation web app that can translate text, Markdown, TXT, PDF, DOCX, and images while preserving Markdown formatting as much as possible.

Usage Tutorial#

1. Environment Preparation#

The base environment specified by the README is:

  • Python 3.10+
  • Recommended to use Conda environment AI
  • Node.js 18+: Only required if you need to use the sibling ../ai-companion/ repository
  • Website and translation functions require a local inference engine: Ollama is preferred; Linux can use vLLM, Windows can fall back to transformers
  • The translation model tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B will be downloaded automatically upon first use

If using Conda:

conda activate AI

Tool settings are located in the root directory config.json, and the README instructions should be copied from config.example.json. This configuration file’s path can be overridden by environment variables:

GADGET_CONFIG

Do not commit the following to Git:

  • API keys and initialization tables within tokens/
  • outputs/
  • build/
  • gadget.egg-info/
  • Deployment repositories and theme repositories under tools/website/
  • Auto-generated content and data synchronized via rclone

2. Install Dependencies#

First, install shared packages and common tool dependencies in the repository root:

pip install -e ".[all]"

Note: all does not include the translator. If you need the translator, install it separately:

pip install -e ".[translator]"

If only using the website function:

pip install -e ".[website]"

Each tool directory also has its corresponding requirements.txt, which can be consulted when needed.

3. LLM and Translation Backend Configuration#

Supported unified LLM backends include:

  • ollama: Default, local Ollama, no API Key required
  • claude_cli: Reuses Claude Code CLI login status, no API Key required
  • anthropic
  • openai

Switching can be done via the --api parameter of each tool, or set globally:

GADGET_LLM_BACKEND

The translation function uses a local inference backend, which can be selected via the following environment variables:

GADGET_TRANSLATION_BACKEND

The default selection order provided in the README is:

ollama → llamacpp / vllm / transformers

The default model is:

tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B

The translation model can be replaced via the following environment variables:

GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL

4. Using the Conversation Summary Tool: Summarize#

This tool employs a two-stage, multi-device workflow:

  1. Export conversation logs on each device.
  2. Synchronize aggregated data via cloud drive or manual copying, and merge by date.
  3. Generate daily reports, then generate weekly and monthly reports.

Export all dates that have not yet been exported:

python -m summarize daily export

Sync all dates and merge them day by day:

python -m summarize daily merge --sync-all

Generate weekly reports and deploy:

python -m summarize weekly generate --week 2026-W12 --deploy

Generate monthly reports and deploy:

python -m summarize monthly generate --month 2026-02 --deploy

Execute the complete one-click process from export and merge to weekly/monthly reports and deployment:

python -m summarize auto --deploy

The old entry point remains compatible, but the modular form above is recommended:

python tools/summarize/daily_summary.py
python tools/summarize/weekly_summary.py
python tools/summarize/monthly_summary.py

This tool automatically discovers and summarizes token usage and costs for various Agent CLIs through the source-specific commands of ccusage 20.x. Optional LLM backends are ollama, claude_cli, anthropic, and openai.

5. Using the Paper Research Tool: Research#

The unified entry point is:

python tools/research/research_scout.py

Execute a complete paper discovery process for a specific project: search, three-stage evaluation, and report generation:

python tools/research/research_scout.py report --project my-project

Search for papers using natural language; the tool will automatically route to the appropriate data source:

python tools/research/research_scout.py ask "找 Pieter Abbeel 最近的机器人操作论文"

Generate a profile for a specific researcher:

python tools/research/research_scout.py profile "Sergey Levine"

Analyze citation maps based on arXiv ID or DOI:

python tools/research/research_scout.py citations 2301.12597

Deploy research reports to Hugo:

python tools/research/research_scout.py deploy

The research tool includes four types of capabilities:

  • Paper Discovery: From arXiv, bioRxiv, PubMed, through a three-stage process of rapid screening, deep evaluation, and citation impact analysis.
  • Deep Paper Insights: Downloads full texts via --insight to analyze writing structure, publication strategies, and reusable knowledge, and also matches OpenReview peer reviews.
  • Researcher Profiling: Combines papers and citation data from ArXiv and Semantic Scholar to generate research trajectories, scores, and relationship inferences.
  • Citation Mapping: Performs forward citation and bibliography analysis based on the Semantic Scholar API, with impact interpreted by an LLM.

Its LLM backend can also be switched via --api.

6. Using the Performance Testing Tool: Benchmark#

All commands require entering the tool directory first:

cd tools/benchmark

Run all benchmarks:

python -m benchmark.cli

Test CPU only:

python -m benchmark.cli --cpu-only

Test GPU only:

python -m benchmark.cli --gpu-only

Run tests and generate an HTML report:

python -m benchmark.cli --report

The /benchmark/ for generating reports and publishing to Hugo:```bash python -m benchmark.cli –report –deploy


This tool supports actual GPU testing for NVIDIA CUDA, Apple Silicon MPS, and Intel XPU; OpenCL may only appear in `--info` detection. Results are written to CSV in append mode and will not overwrite existing results, making it suitable for aggregating scores from multiple machines.

---

# 7. Using Hugo Website Tool: Website

Install website-related dependencies:

```bash
pip install -e ".[website]"

Execute incremental compression, Hugo build, and Pages push on macOS or Linux:

cd tools/website && bash update.sh

Execute the corresponding script on Windows:

powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/website/update.ps1

Start the local Hugo preview server, including draft content:

cd tools/website && hugo server -D

The website automatically handles the following tasks:

  • Only compresses media files that have changed since .last_build.
  • Uses pngquant for images and HandBrakeCLI for videos.
  • Automatically generated daily reports, research reports, Benchmark pages, etc., are written directly to the Hugo content root directory.
  • Generated files will carry the gadget_generated tag; handwritten files without this tag will not be overwritten.
  • The build script will automatically commit and push to the independent GitHub Pages deployment repository in tools/website/public/.

Do not commit content directly to tools/website/public/.

8. Using Document Translator: Translator#

Install the translator:

pip install -e ".[translator]"

Start the Gradio GUI:

python -m translator

After starting, the local translation page will open in your browser.

Supported translation formats:

  • Plain text
  • .md
  • .txt
  • .pdf
  • .docx
  • Images

The translator will protect code blocks, URLs, Hugo shortcodes, etc., within Markdown to preserve the original format as much as possible. The source language can be set to auto, which identifies based on the proportion of CJK characters in the text; when the target language is set to auto, it will automatically switch between Chinese and English.

9. Operations and Sync Scripts#

View or execute centralized rclone data synchronization:

python scripts/sync.py

The README explicitly lists the push and pull forms for cross-device synchronization:

python scripts/sync.py push
python scripts/sync.py pull

Sync configuration is located in the sync section of the root directory config.json, and other configuration files can also be specified via GADGET_CONFIG.

One-time initialization process for new machines:

  1. Fill out tokens/onboard.yaml.
  2. Execute:
python scripts/onboard.py

It will complete SSH, Claude/Codex CLI installation and authentication, pip extras, ai-companion, configuration for various tools, and rclone initialization.

Execute a read-only smoke test that produces no network, LLM calls, or writes:

bash scripts/smoke.sh

Create an Ollama variant optimized for summarize and output environment configurations:

eval "$(bash scripts/serve_local_llm.sh env)"

For system-level installation of SSH public keys, Claude Code, Codex, Superpowers, Ponytail, and AI Companion on Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 servers, refer to the scripts in the peer repository for help:

bash ../ai-companion/scripts/onboard-server.sh --help

Gadget is a collection of practical development tools composed of multiple independent tools, covering:

  • AI conversation daily, weekly, and monthly report generation
  • Academic paper discovery and researcher analysis
  • CPU/GPU performance benchmarking

gadget/
├── tools/

Target Directory

3. Tool Functions#

summarize#

Reads AI conversation logs from sources such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor Agent, ChatGPT, etc., and calls LLMs to generate:

  • Daily reports
  • Weekly reports
  • Monthly reports and trend summaries

It uses a multi-device two-stage process:

  1. Each device exports conversation logs
  2. Aggregates data and generates reports by day

Simultaneously, it uses ccusage to statistics token usage and costs for different Agent CLIs.

Supports four LLM backends:

  • ollama：Default, local Ollama, no API Key required
  • claude_cli：Reuses Claude Code login status
  • anthropic
  • openai

research#

An academic research tool containing four types of capabilities:

  • Paper Discovery: Searches arXiv, bioRxiv, PubMed, and performs a three-stage LLM evaluation
  • Deep Paper Insights: Analyzes paper writing structure, publication strategies, core knowledge, and OpenReview reviews
  • Researcher Profiling: Combines ArXiv and Semantic Scholar data to analyze research trajectories, citations, and mentor-student relationships
  • Citation Mapping: Analyzes forward citations and backward references of papers

benchmark#

A cross-platform CPU/GPU floating-point performance testing tool.

Supports:

  • NVIDIA CUDA
  • Apple Silicon MPS
  • Intel XPU

Supports multiple precisions, including FP64, FP32, FP16, BF16, and experimental FP8.

Results are appended to CSV and will not overwrite historical data; it can also generate Plotly interactive HTML reports and leaderboards.

website#

A Hugo-based blog site using the PaperMod theme, published to GitHub Pages.

Main features:

  • Incremental compression of images and videos
  • Automatic translation of bilingual content
  • Automatic building of the Hugo website
  • Automatic commit and push of the deployment repository

Writing website content:

tools/website/content
tools/website/static

tools/website/public/ is a separate deployment repository and should not be committed directly to the current project.

translator#

A local document translator based on Gradio, supporting:

  • Text
  • Markdown
  • TXT
  • PDF
  • DOCX
  • Images

It protects Markdown code blocks, URLs, Hugo shortcodes, and other content. It uses the local model tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B by default and also supports GGUF versions.

The translation backend is automatically selected by the shared translation engine:

  • Ollama
  • vLLM
  • transformers
  • llama.cpp/GGUF

outputs/#

outputs/

Gadget is a collection of practical tools accumulated during daily development, covering scenarios such as AI conversation daily/weekly/monthly report generation, paper discovery and researcher analysis, performance benchmarking, Hugo blog automation, document translation, etc.

Its core design is: each directory under tools/ is a tool that can be used independently; the common/ in the repository root is a shared infrastructure package, installed via pip install -e ., providing common capabilities like LLM calling, JSON parsing, disk caching, atomic writing, translation, Hugo deployment, etc., to each tool. ├── images/       # 图表和生成图片
└── backups/      # 强制覆盖备份

Hugo website content is not written to outputs/site first, but is written directly to tools/website/content|static by the deployment process.

Roles of Each Tool

tools/summarize/：AI conversation report generation tool.
Automatically reads AI conversation records from Claude Code, Codex, Cursor Agent, ChatGPT, general JSON, etc., and calls LLMs to generate daily, weekly, and monthly trend summaries. Supports multi-device workflows: each device exports conversation logs, aggregates them via cloud drives or manual copying, and then generates the final report. Uses ccusage 20.x to statistics token usage and costs for each agent CLI. LLM backends can be switched uniformly via --api, including ollama, claude_cli, anthropic, and openai.

tools/research/：Academic research tool.
The unified entry point is tools/research/research_scout.py, providing four types of capabilities: paper discovery, deep paper insights, researcher profiling, and citation graph analysis. Supports arXiv, bioRxiv, PubMed, Semantic Scholar, and uses LLMs to complete filtering, evaluation, impact analysis, writing structure analysis, research trajectory analysis, etc.

tools/benchmark/：CPU/GPU performance benchmarking tool.
Cross-platform measurement of floating-point performance under different hardware and precision levels, supporting actual GPU execution for NVIDIA CUDA, Apple Silicon MPS, and Intel XPU. Results are appended to CSV, and it can generate Plotly interactive HTML reports and leaderboards, as well as support deployment to Hugo websites.

tools/website/：Hugo blog site.
This is the Hugo static blog “TzJ’s Net”, using the PaperMod theme, deployed to GitHub Pages. It features an incremental image/video compression workflow, using pngquant for images and HandBrakeCLI for videos. Automatically generated content is written to tools/website/content|static with a gadget_generated mark; handwritten files without this mark will not be overwritten. tools/website/public/ is a separate deployment repository and should not be committed directly.

tools/translator/：Gradio document translator.
Based on the common translation engine, it provides a local translation webpage similar to Google Translate. Supports translating text and files such as .md, .txt, .pdf, .docx, and images, while attempting to preserve Markdown formatting and protecting code blocks, URLs, Hugo shortcodes, etc. The default model is tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B, with a GGUF variant tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B-GGUF.

common/：Shared infrastructure.
Provides capabilities such as unified LLM calling, JSON parsing and repair, SHA-256 disk caching, atomic writing, content hashing, local inference translation engine, bilingual content generation, and cross-platform Hugo deployment.

scripts/：Operations and maintenance scripts.
Includes sync.py data synchronization, onboard.py new machine initialization, smoke.sh read-only smoke checks, serve_local_llm.sh local Ollama variant configuration, language.py Hugo bilingual auditing and report renaming, profile_translation.py translation engine GPU profiling, etc.

../ai-companion/：Independent repository.
Does not belong to the gadget repository itself. It is responsible for function-level code change records, testing and HTML report generation, the /idea→/ccplan→/ccedit planning and execution workflow, and Claude Code skills.

II. Chinese Usage Tutorial

1. Environment Preparation

The basic requirements listed in the README are as follows:

# Python 版本要求
Python 3.10+

It is recommended to use the conda environment AI:

conda activate AI

If you need to use the adjacent ../ai-companion/ repository, you will need:

Node.js 18+

Specific dependencies for each tool can be found in the corresponding requirements.txt directory.

If you need to perform a full installation of extras for common, summarize, research, benchmark, and website, you can run the following in the repository root:```bash pip install -e “.[all]”


Note: `all` does not include `translator`. The translator needs to be installed separately:

```bash
pip install -e ".[translator]"

The website and translation functions use a local inference engine. The README states that Ollama is used by default; vLLM is available on Linux, and transformers is available as a fallback on Windows. Model tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B will be automatically downloaded upon the first run.

2. Configuration Preparation

Tool configuration is located in config.json at the repository root, which is gitignored. The README explains that it should be copied from config.example.json.

If you need to override the configuration file path, you can set:

GADGET_CONFIG

The LLM backend can be switched via the --api parameter of each tool. The optional backends mentioned in the README are:

ollama
claude_cli
anthropic
openai

Global environment variables can also be used:

GADGET_LLM_BACKEND

The translation backend is controlled by the following environment variable:

GADGET_TRANSLATION_BACKEND

The README states that the translation path defaults to using the local Ollama server, and subsequently can use llamacpp / vllm / transformers. The translation model can be overridden via the following environment variable:

GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL

The API key and onboarding table are located in the tokens/ directory, which is gitignored. The README specifically warns not to commit its contents.

3. Installation

Install the shared package and main tool dependencies in the repository root:

pip install -e ".[all]"

If you want to use the document translator, install the translator extras:

pip install -e ".[translator]"

If you only target the website functionality, the installation command provided in the README is:

pip install -e ".[website]"

4. New Machine Initialization

The README mentions that new machine configuration can use scripts/onboard.py. The process involves first filling out:

tokens/onboard.yaml

Then running:

python scripts/onboard.py

It will complete SSH configuration, Claude/Codex CLI installation and authentication, pip extras, ai-companion installation, tool configurations, rclone bootstrap, etc.

Server-level system installation has been migrated to ../ai-companion/:

bash ../ai-companion/scripts/onboard-server.sh --help

5. Data Synchronization

Cross-device data synchronization uses scripts/sync.py and requires rclone configuration.

The general way to run it provided in the README is:

python scripts/sync.py

It also mentions that cross-device synchronization can use:

python scripts/sync.py push
python scripts/sync.py pull

Configuration is located in the sync section of config.json at the repository root; the configuration path can also be overridden using GADGET_CONFIG.

If you only want to sync data, the README explicitly states in the repository structure section:

python scripts/sync.py

6. Summarize: AI Daily, Weekly, and Monthly Reports

This tool recommends using the new module entry point:

python -m summarize

A typical workflow is as follows.

Export all dates that have not yet been exported:

python -m summarize daily export

Sync all dates and merge them day by day:

python -m summarize daily merge --sync-all

Generate and deploy a weekly report for a specific week:

python -m summarize weekly generate --week 2026-W12 --deploy

Generate and deploy a monthly report for a specific month:

python -m summarize monthly generate --month 2026-02 --deploy

Execute the full process with one click: Export, merge, weekly report, monthly report, and deploy:

python -m summarize auto --deploy

The old entry point is still compatible:

python tools/summarize/daily_summary.py ...
python tools/summarize/weekly_summary.py ...
python tools/summarize/monthly_summary.py ...

But the README recommends using:

python -m summarize

The LLM backend can be switched uniformly via --api. Values listed in the README include:

ollama
claude_cli
anthropic
openai

7. Research: Paper Discovery, Researcher Analysis, Citation Graphs

The unified entry point is:

python tools/research/research_scout.py

Run the full paper discovery process: Search, three-stage evaluation, and report generation:

python tools/research/research_scout.py report --project my-project

Natural language search; the tool will automatically route the source:

python tools/research/research_scout.py ask "找 Pieter Abbeel 最近的机器人操作论文"

Generate researcher profiles:

python tools/research/research_scout.py profile "Sergey Levine"

Perform citation graph analysis by arXiv ID or DOI:

python tools/research/research_scout.py citations 2301.12597

Deploy research reports to Hugo:

python tools/research/research_scout.py deploy

All LLM functions also support switching backends via --api:

ollama
claude_cli
anthropic
openai

8. Benchmark: CPU/GPU Performance Benchmarking

The README explicitly states that all benchmark commands require entering tools/benchmark/ first:

cd tools/benchmark

Run all benchmarks and append results to a CSV:

python -m benchmark.cli

Run CPU only:

python -m benchmark.cli --cpu-only

Run GPU only:

python -m benchmark.cli --gpu-only

Run benchmarks and generate an HTML report:

python -m benchmark.cli --report

Generate a report and publish it to the Hugo /benchmark/:

python -m benchmark.cli --report --deploy

The README explains that the tool will automatically detect CUDA, Apple MPS, and Intel XPU. OpenCL might only appear in the --info detection, but the README does not provide specific command examples for --info.

9. Website: Hugo Blog

Install website dependencies:

pip install -e ".[website]"

Incremental compression, Hugo build, and push to GitHub Pages under macOS/Linux:

cd tools/website && bash update.sh

Run the PowerShell script under Windows; the script will switch to its own directory:

powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/website/update.ps1

Local preview, including drafts:

cd tools/website && hugo server -D

The README specifically notes:

tools/website/public/ is a separate deployment repository tzj2006/tzj2006.github.io, which is automatically committed and pushed by the build script; do not commit it directly.

Automatically generated content will be written to:

tools/website/content
tools/website/static

Files marked with gadget_generated can be managed by the automated process; handwritten files without this mark will not be overwritten.

10. Translator: Gradio Document Translator

Install translator dependencies:

pip install -e ".[translator]"

Start the Gradio GUI:

python -m translator

After starting, the interface will open in a browser.

It supports translating text and files. File types listed in the README include:

.md
.txt
.pdf
.docx
images

Default model:

tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B

GGUF variants:

tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B-GGUF

The model can be overridden via environment variables:

GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL

The source language can be set to auto via text CJK ratio detection; when the target language is auto, it will automatically switch between Chinese and English.

11. Smoke Checks and Local LLM Helper Scripts

Run a read-only smoke check:

bash scripts/smoke.sh

The README explains that this script checks the --help, --info, and imports of each tool, without triggering LLM, network, or write operations.

Create a summarize-tuned Ollama variant and print environment variables:

eval "$(bash scripts/serve_local_llm.sh env)"

Persistent configuration is placed in the summarize section of config.json at the repository root; the path can also be overridden using GADGET_CONFIG.

12. Usage Notes

Do not commit these contents:

tokens/
outputs/
build/
gadget.egg-info/
tools/website/ 下的部署仓库或 theme repo
自动生成内容
rclone 同步数据

  • outputs/ saves all generated files; it is gitignored.
  • build/ and gadget.egg-info/ are build artifacts generated by pip install -e ..
  • Cross-device synchronization depends on rclone.
  • The project license is GPL-3, see LICENSE.

I. Project Summary#

1. What is this#

gadget (Gadgets) is a set of practical tools accumulated by the author during daily development, covering five directions:

  • AI Conversation Daily Reports
  • Paper Discovery
  • Performance Benchmarking
  • Blog Automation
  • Document Translation

Each directory under tools/ is an independent tool that can be used separately. All tools share the common/ package in the repository root, which provides capabilities such as LLM calling, JSON parsing, disk caching, atomic writing, translation, and Hugo deployment, installed via pip install -e ..

The development workflow (planning, execution, change tracking) and all Claude Code skills are not in this repository; they are provided by another repository, ai-companion. It is located in the sibling directory ../ai-companion/ and integrates with this repository through hooks under .claude/ and .codex/.

2. Repository Structure#

gadget/
├── tools/              # 五个独立工具
│   ├── summarize/      # AI 对话日报 / 周报 / 月报
│   ├── research/       # 论文发现 + 研究者分析 + 引用图谱
│   ├── benchmark/      # CPU/GPU 性能基准测试
│   ├── website/        # Hugo 博客（增量媒体压缩 + 自动构建发布）
│   └── translator/     # Gradio 文档翻译器
├── common/             # 共享基础设施包，所有工具都依赖它
├── scripts/            # 运维与维护脚本（sync.py、onboard.py、smoke.sh 等）
├── docs/               # 设计文档、ECL 计划（docs/ecl/）、审计报告、历史归档
├── outputs/            # 所有生成产物（已 gitignore，可自动重建）

Supports a two-stage multi-device workflow: export from each device first, then aggregate and merge. Uses ccusage 20.x to statistics token usage and costs for each agent CLI | Claude/OpenAI API, ccusage, matplotlib | | research | Unified entry point is research_scout.py, providing four capabilities: ① Paper discovery (three-stage LLM evaluation for arXiv, bioRxiv, PubMed, generating research weekly reports); ② Deep paper insights --insight (download full text, analyze writing structure, match OpenReview review comments); ③ Researcher profiling (research trajectory, tier scoring, mentor-student relationship discovery, name disambiguation); ④ Citation mapping (forward citation and backward reference analysis) | arXiv/bioRxiv/PubMed, Semantic Scholar, LLM | | benchmark | Cross-platform CPU/GPU FLOPS testing.
