What each tool does#

tools/summarize/
Automatically reads daily AI conversation logs (Claude Code / Codex / Cursor Agent / ChatGPT / general JSON) and calls an LLM to generate structured daily/weekly/monthly reports. Multi-device two-stage process: each device first exports, then aggregates via cloud drive sync or manual copy before generating daily reports; once enough daily reports are collected, weekly and monthly trends are generated. Automatically discovers and statistics token usage and costs for various agent CLIs through ccusage 20.x source-based commands (ccusage claude, ccusage codex, ccusage gemini…). Four summary backends can be switched uniformly using --api: ollama (default, local, keyless, Qwen3.8-27B), claude_cli (reuses Claude Code CLI login state, no API key required), anthropic, openai.

tools/research/
A unified academic research toolbox with a single entry point tools/research/research_scout.py, offering four capabilities:

  1. Paper Discovery: Searches arXiv / bioRxiv / PubMed via a three-stage LLM pipeline (fast screening → deep evaluation → citation impact analysis), generates research weekly reports, and deploys them to Hugo; supports conference paper search and author search.
  2. Deep Paper Insights (--insight): Downloads full texts, analyzes writing structure, publication strategies, and reusable core knowledge; automatically matches OpenReview reviewer comments; synthesizes research writing guides across papers.
  3. Researcher Profiling: Pulls papers and citations from ArXiv + Semantic Scholar; LLM generates research trajectory analysis and calculates graded scores; automatically discovers mentor-student relationships via homepage extraction + co-authorship patterns; supports name disambiguation and reverse lookup.
  4. Citation Graph Analysis: Performs forward citation / backward reference analysis based on the Semantic Scholar API, combined with LLM for impact interpretation.

LLM switching also uses --api, with the same four backends as summarize.

tools/benchmark/
Cross-platform CPU/GPU FLOPS benchmark, unifying floating-point performance measurements across different hardware vendors and precision levels. Actual GPU execution supports NVIDIA (CUDA), Apple Silicon (MPS), and Intel (XPU) (OpenCL may only appear in --info detection). Precision coverage includes FP64 / FP32 / FP16 / BF16 / FP8 (experimental). Measurement process: Warm-up + formal measurement + statistical analysis (median, IQR for outlier removal), with explicit GPU synchronization to ensure timing accuracy. Results are written to CSV in append mode (not overwriting, naturally supporting cumulative multi-hardware leaderboards), can generate interactive HTML reports and leaderboards with Plotly charts, and can be deployed to Hugo or submitted to public leaderboards.tools/website/
Hugo static blog site (“TzJ’s Net”, PaperMod theme), deployed to GitHub Pages (https://tzj2006.github.io/). Features built-in incremental image/video compression (only compresses media changed since .last_build: images via pngquant, videos via HandBrakeCLI), as well as local model bilingual translation (default Ollama; fallback to vLLM on Linux, transformers on Windows; model tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B is automatically downloaded on first run, without using cloud LLM APIs). Each tool’s deploy pipeline writes automatically generated content directly into tools/website/content|static (the unique Hugo content root; marked with gadget_generated; handwritten files without this mark are never overwritten), then translates, compresses, builds, and pushes. tools/website/public/ is a standalone deployment repository (tzj2006/tzj2006.github.io), which is automatically committed + pushed by build scripts—do not commit directly to it.

tools/translator/
A Gradio document translator based on the common translation engine: a Google Translate-like local web interface that translates text and files (.md / .txt / .pdf / .docx / images) while preserving Markdown formatting (code blocks, URLs, Hugo shortcodes, etc., are protected). Local inference, no cloud APIs used. Automatically selects the backend via common.engine.create_engine() (prioritizes ollama when model tags are pulled; falls back to transformers on Windows; prioritizes vllm on Linux; uses llamacpp for GGUF with low VRAM), with models kept in memory (warm) and lazy-loaded on demand when switching models. Default model is tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B (GGUF variant tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B-GGUF), automatically downloaded on first use, which can be overridden by GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL or the in-GUI model management. Source language can be set to auto (detected by CJK text ratio); when the target is auto, it flips between zh↔en.

common/
The shared layer relied upon by all tools: unified two-layer LLM API (four backends), JSON parsing and repair, SHA-256 disk caching (namespace + TTL), atomic writes and content hashing, local inference translation engine and bilingual content generation, and cross-platform Hugo deployment.

scripts/
Operations scripts: rclone data synchronization, new machine onboarding, read-only smoke tests, local LLM environment setup, Hugo bilingual auditing, translation engine GPU profiler, etc.

../ai-companion/ (standalone repository)
Records function-level code changes, generates tests and HTML reports, provides a /idea→/ccplan→/ccedit plan-execute pipeline, and hosts all Claude Code skills. It is also packaged as a standard Claude Code plugin and an equivalent Codex integration, ready to use upon installation. This repository no longer contains the skills/ directory.

outputs/
All artifacts are centralized here (gitignored, can be automatically rebuilt): logs/, reports/, cache/, data/, images/, backups/. Hugo site content is written directly to tools/website/content|static, with no separate outputs/site staging tree.

2. Usage Tutorial for First-Timers#

2.1 Environment Preparation#

Requirements provided in README:

  • Python 3.10+ (recommended conda environment AI)
  • Node.js 18+ (only required by the standalone repository ../ai-companion/)
  • Specific dependencies for each tool can be found in the corresponding directory’s requirements.txt
  • Website/translation features use local inference engines (default Ollama; fallback to vLLM on Linux, transformers on Windows); model tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B is automatically downloaded on first run.

Activate the recommended environment:

conda activate AI

Additionally, please read the AGENTS.md (workflow protocol for all AI agents before they act) and CLAUDE.md (Claude Code repository guide) in the repository root. For more detailed step-by-step instructions, see TUTORIAL.md.

2.2 Installation#

Install the shared package common/ and tool extras in the repository root.

Install common + summarize / research / benchmark / website extras (excluding translator):

pip install -e ".[all]"

Install translator separately (all does not include translator):

pip install -e ".[translator]"

Install only website-related dependencies (includes torch + transformers for translation):

pip install -e ".[website]"

pip install -e . will generate build/ and gadget.egg-info/ in the repository root (already gitignored).

For ai-companion installation, see ../ai-companion/scripts/install.ts. It serves as both a Claude Code plugin and a Codex integration, ready to use upon installation without needing a build step.

2.3 Configuration#

Repository-level Configuration

  • Tool settings are located in config.json in the repository root (already gitignored).
  • Copy from config.example.json before making changes.
  • Paths can be overridden using the GADGET_CONFIG environment variable.

Keys and Onboarding Table

  • tokens/ stores API keys and the onboarding table, which is gitignored—never commit its contents.

One-time Configuration for New Machines (this repository)

  1. Fill out a YAML file: tokens/onboard.yaml
  2. Run scripts/onboard.py once

It will automatically complete: SSH configuration, Claude/Codex CLI installation and authentication, pip extras and ai-companion installation, tool configurations, and rclone bootstrap.

System-level Installation for New Servers (Ubuntu 22.04/24.04)

Scripts have been migrated to ai-companion: ../ai-companion/scripts/onboard-server.sh. After the repository split, --companion-repo is passed directly to the ai-companion repository (git@github.com:TzJ2006/ai-companion.git), and --companion-ref is no longer required. Usage:

bash ../ai-companion/scripts/onboard-server.sh --help

LLM Backends (Global)

Use --api to switch uniformly: ollama (default), claude_cli, anthropic, openai. You can also globally specify via the GADGET_LLM_BACKEND environment variable.

Translation Backend / Models

  • The backend is selected by GADGET_TRANSLATION_BACKEND: ollama (default when models are already pulled, uses local Ollama service) → llamacpp / vllm / transformers (in-process).
  • Models: tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B; the translator can also be overridden by GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL or the in-GUI model management.

Cross-device Data Synchronization

rclone must be configured first. Configuration is located in the sync section of the repository root’s config.json (paths can also be overridden by GADGET_CONFIG).

python scripts/sync.py
python scripts/sync.py push
python scripts/sync.py pull

The README specifies that sync.py overrides categories such as summarize / website / research / benchmark / backups, and includes a special dag category (generates and deploys DAG sites); subcommands also include status / bootstrap / config.

Content Not to be Committed

Do not git add: automatically generated content, rclone sync data, build artifacts (build/, gadget.egg-info/), and deployment/theme repositories under tools/website/. All generated files are in outputs/ (already gitignored). License is GPL-3 (see LICENSE).

Post-installation Read-only Smoke Check (does not call LLMs, does not connect to the internet, does not write files):

bash scripts/smoke.sh

Local Ollama variant for summarize (prints environment variables for eval):

eval "$(bash scripts/serve_local_llm.sh env)"

Persistence knobs are written in the summarize section of the repository root’s config.json (paths can be overridden by GADGET_CONFIG).

Other operations scripts: language.py (Hugo bilingual audit + summarize report renaming), profile_translation.py (translation engine GPU profiler).

2.4 Typical Usage for Each Tool#

Summarize: AI Daily/Weekly/Monthly Reports#

Multi-device workflow: Each device first exports unexported dates → sync and merge by day → once enough daily reports are gathered, generate weekly/monthly reports. The recommended new entry point is python -m summarize (old entry points python tools/summarize/daily_summary.py ... / weekly_summary.py / monthly_summary.py are still available but use a compatibility re-export shim).

python -m summarize daily export                                   # 阶段 1：导出所有未导出日期
python -m summarize daily merge --sync-all                         # 阶段 2：同步全部日期并按天合并
python -m summarize weekly generate --week 2026-W12 --deploy       # 周报 + 部署
python -m summarize monthly generate --month 2026-02 --deploy      # 月报 + 部署
python -m summarize auto --deploy                                  # 一键全流水线：export → merge → weekly → monthly + deploy

Switch LLM backends using --api (ollama / claude_cli / anthropic / openai). For more detailed steps, see the Summarize section of TUTORIAL.md and tools/summarize/tutorial.md.

Research: Paper Discovery and Researcher Analysis#

The unified entry point is tools/research/research_scout.py.

python tools/research/research_scout.py report --project my-project        # 全流水线：检索 → 三阶段评估 → 报告
python tools/research/research_scout.py ask "找 Pieter Abbeel 最近的机器人操作论文"  # 自然语言搜索（自动路由数据源）
python tools/research/research_scout.py profile "Sergey Levine"             # 研究者画像
python tools/research/research_scout.py citations 2301.12597               # 引用图（按 arXiv ID / DOI）
python tools/research/research_scout.py deploy                              # 把报告部署到 Hugo

Deep paper insight capabilities are marked in the README as --insight, but a complete, copyable command line is not provided. LLMs are also switched across four backends using --api. For more detailed steps, see the Research section of TUTORIAL.md and tools/research/TUTORIAL.md.

Benchmark: Performance Benchmark SuiteNote: All commands must first go through cd into tools/benchmark/. The GPU will automatically detect CUDA / Apple MPS / Intel XPU. Results are written to CSV in append mode and will not be overwritten.#

cd tools/benchmark
python -m benchmark.cli                # 跑全部基准（结果追加到 CSV）
python -m benchmark.cli --cpu-only     # 只测 CPU
python -m benchmark.cli --gpu-only     # 只测 GPU
python -m benchmark.cli --report       # 跑基准 + 生成 HTML 报告
python -m benchmark.cli --report --deploy  # 生成报告并发布到 Hugo /benchmark/

--info will perform detection (OpenCL may only appear in the detection results). For more detailed steps, see the Benchmark section of TUTORIAL.md and tools/benchmark/tutorial.md.

Website: Hugo Blog#

Automatically generated content is written to tools/website/content|static by each tool’s deploy pipeline, then translated, compressed, built, and pushed. tools/website/public/ is an independent deployment repository, which is automatically committed and pushed by build scripts; do not commit directly into it.

pip install -e ".[website]"                          # 安装依赖（含翻译用的 torch + transformers）
cd tools/website && bash update.sh                   # macOS/Linux：增量压缩 + Hugo 构建 + 推送 Pages
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/website/update.ps1  # Windows（脚本会自己 cd 到所在目录）
cd tools/website && hugo server -D                   # 本地预览（开发服务器，含草稿）

For more detailed steps, see the Website section of TUTORIAL.md and tools/website/CLAUDE.md.

Translator: Gradio Document Translator#

Local inference; default models are automatically downloaded upon first use. The source language can be set to auto; when the target is auto, it flips between Chinese and English.

pip install -e ".[translator]"   # 安装依赖（gradio + GGUF 翻译栈）
python -m translator             # 启动 Gradio GUI（在浏览器打开）

For more detailed steps, see the Translator section of TUTORIAL.md. UI wiring is in tools/translator/app.py, translation and file logic is in tools/translator/core.py, and the shared engine is in common/engine.py and common/translation.py.

2.5 Suggested First-Time Onboarding Order#

Strictly following the path that can be connected via README:

  1. conda activate AI, confirm Python 3.10+. If you want to use ai-companion, prepare Node.js 18+ as well.
  2. Copy config.json from config.example.json; when keys are required, place them only in tokens/, do not commit them.
  3. New machine: fill tokens/onboard.yaml, run scripts/onboard.py. For new Ubuntu servers, you can also check bash ../ai-companion/scripts/onboard-server.sh --help.
  4. pip install -e ".[all]"; if you want to use the translation GUI, then pip install -e ".[translator]".
  5. bash scripts/smoke.sh for read-only smoke testing.
  6. Use individual tools according to the commands in each section above; for cross-device data, use python scripts/sync.py push / pull (requires rclone).
  7. To change tool logic, go to tools/<tool>/; to change shared capabilities, go to common/; to change workflows/skills, go to ../ai-companion/.

For more step-by-step operations, configurations, data formats, and FAQs, the README explicitly points to TUTORIAL.md and the source documentation of each tool; this tutorial does not use extra commands from those files.

  2. Deep Paper Insights (--insight): Downloads full text, analyzes writing structure/publication strategy/reusable knowledge; matches OpenReview to obtain reviewer comments; synthesizes cross-paper writing guides.
  3. Researcher Profiling: Uses ArXiv + Semantic Scholar data, LLM generates research trajectory analysis and hierarchical scoring; extracts mentor-student relationships through homepage and co-authorship patterns; supports name disambiguation and reverse lookup.
  4. Citation Graph Analysis: Based on Semantic Scholar for forward citation/backward reference analysis + LLM impact interpretation.

Benchmark — Performance Benchmarking Suite#

  • Cross-platform CPU/GPU FLOPS benchmarking.
  • Supports NVIDIA (CUDA), Apple Silicon (MPS), Intel (XPU).
  • Precision: FP64 / FP32 / FP16 / BF16 / FP8 (experimental).
  • Warm-up + formal measurement + statistical analysis (median, IQR outlier removal).
  • Results appended to CSV; can generate interactive HTML reports and leaderboards; can be deployed to Hugo or submitted to public leaderboards.

Website — Hugo Blog#

  • Static blog “TzJ’s Net” (PaperMod theme), deployed to GitHub Pages: https://tzj2006.github.io/.
  • Incremental image/video compression (pngquant, HandBrakeCLI).
  • Local model bilingual translation (default Ollama; Linux fallback vLLM, Windows fallback transformers; model tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B is automatically downloaded upon first run).
  • Automatically generated content is written to tools/website/content|static (with gadget_generated markers; hand-written files will not be overwritten).
  • tools/website/public/ is an independent deployment repository (tzj2006/tzj2006.github.io), which is automatically committed and pushed by build scripts; do not commit directly into it.

Translator — Gradio Document Translator#

  • Local inference Web UI based on the common translation engine.
  • Supports text and files (.md / .txt / .pdf / .docx / images), preserving Markdown format.
  • Automatic backend selection: prioritizes ollama, Windows fallback to transformers, Linux prioritizes vllm, low VRAM option llamacpp.
  • Default model tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B; can be overridden by GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL or GUI.
  • Source language auto is detected by CJK ratio; target auto toggles between zh↔en.

5. common / scripts / ai-companion#

common/: LLM calls, JSON parsing fixes, SHA-256 disk caching, atomic writes, local translation engine, cross-platform Hugo deployment.

scripts/ main scripts:| Script | Role | |——|——| | sync.py | rclone data synchronization (push/pull/status/bootstrap/config) | | onboard.py | One-time configuration for new machines | | smoke.sh | Read-only smoke test (--help / --info / imports) | | serve_local_llm.sh | Create summarize-tuned Ollama variants and print environment variables | | language.py | Hugo bilingual audit + summarize report renaming | | profile_translation.py | Translation engine GPU profiling |

ai-companion: An independent Node.js repository providing code change tracking, planning/execution pipelines, and all Claude Code skills; see ../ai-companion/scripts/install.ts for installation.

II. Detailed Chinese Usage Tutorial (First-time Setup)#

Step 0: Understand Output and Configuration Locations#

Generated Artifacts Directory (gitignored, rebuildable):

outputs/
├── logs/         # 中间产物（导出日志、运行日志）
├── reports/      # 最终报告（Markdown、JSON、HTML）
├── cache/        # LLM 缓存、搜索缓存
├── data/         # 结构化数据（CSV、JSON profiles）
├── images/       # 图表与生成图片
└── backups/      # 强制覆盖备份

Hugo site content is written directly to tools/website/content|static (no separate outputs/site).

Configuration:

  • Tool settings: Repository root config.json (gitignored; copy from config.example.json)
  • Available environment variables GADGET_CONFIG override configuration paths
  • API keys and onboarding tables: tokens/ (gitignored, DO NOT commit)

Step 1: Environment Preparation#

Basic Requirements:

  • Python 3.10+ (Recommended conda environment AI: conda activate AI)
  • Node.js 18+ (Only required for ../ai-companion/)

Install Dependencies:

# common + summarize / research / benchmark / website（all 不含 translator）
pip install -e ".[all]"

# translator 需单独安装
pip install -e ".[translator]"

# website 单独安装（含 torch + transformers，用于翻译）
pip install -e ".[website]"

LLM Backend (Global):

  • Switch between tools uniformly using --api: ollama (default), claude_cli, anthropic, openai
  • Also available via environment variable GADGET_LLM_BACKEND

Translation Backend:

  • Environment variable GADGET_TRANSLATION_BACKEND
  • Default ollama (if model is already pulled); also llamacpp / vllm / transformers
  • Default model tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B, automatically downloaded on first run

Local LLM (summarize related):

eval "$(bash scripts/serve_local_llm.sh env)"

Persistent parameters are written in the summarize section of config.json (use GADGET_CONFIG to override path).

Step 2: One-time Configuration for New Machines (Recommended)#

Method A — Local Repository Machine Configuration:

  1. Fill in tokens/onboard.yaml
  2. Run:
python scripts/onboard.py

Will automatically complete: SSH, Claude/Codex CLI installation and authentication, pip extras, ai-companion installation, tool configurations, and rclone bootstrap.

Method B — Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 Server System-level Installation:

Migrated to the ai-companion repository:

bash ../ai-companion/scripts/onboard-server.sh --help

Requires passing --companion-repo git@github.com:TzJ2006/ai-companion.git (no longer requires --companion-ref).

Smoke Test (Read-only, no disk writing, no LLM calls, no internet):

bash scripts/smoke.sh

Step 3: Data Synchronization (Multi-device / Multi-machine)#

python scripts/sync.py
  • Configured in the sync section of the repository root config.json
  • Use GADGET_CONFIG to override configuration paths
  • Cross-device synchronization example:
python scripts/sync.py push
python scripts/sync.py pull

(Requires rclone configuration.)

Step 4: Summarize — AI Daily/Weekly/Monthly Conversation Reports#

Typical Workflow (Recommended new entry python -m summarize):

# 阶段 1：导出所有未导出日期
python -m summarize daily export

# 阶段 2：同步所有日期并按天合并
python -m summarize daily merge --sync-all

# 周报 + 部署
python -m summarize weekly generate --week 2026-W12 --deploy

# 月报 + 部署
python -m summarize monthly generate --month 2026-02 --deploy

# 一键全流程：export → merge → weekly → monthly + deploy
python -m summarize auto --deploy

Old Entry (still available, compatible via shim):

python tools/summarize/weekly_summary.py ...
python tools/summarize/monthly_summary.py ...

Step 5: Research — Paper Discovery and Research Analysis#

Unified CLI: tools/research/research_scout.py

# 自然语言搜索（自动路由数据源）
python tools/research/research_scout.py ask "找 Pieter Abbeel 最近的机器人操作论文"

LLM backend also uses --api: ollama (default), claude_cli, anthropic, openai.

For more detailed steps, see TUTORIAL.md#research and tools/research/TUTORIAL.md.

Step 6: Benchmark — CPU/GPU Performance Testing#

Note: All commands must first enter tools/benchmark/:

cd tools/benchmark

# 运行全部基准（结果追加到 CSV）

# 仅 CPU

Build and Publish:

pip install -e ".[translator]"

Open the Gradio GUI in your browser after starting. For more detailed instructions, see TUTORIAL.md#translator; implementation can be found in tools/translator/app.py, tools/translator/core.py, common/engine.py, and common/translation.py.

Part I: Open Source Project Gadgets Summary#

1. Project Introduction#

Gadgets is a collection of practical tools accumulated during daily development, covering five core areas: AI Daily/Weekly/Monthly Conversation Report Generation, Academic Paper Discovery and Scholar Analysis, Hardware/Software Performance Benchmarking, Automated Hugo Personal Blog Construction and Publishing, and Local Document Translation.

  • Architectural Features: Each tool under the tools/ directory is independent and can be used separately; general infrastructure (such as LLM calls, JSON parsing, disk caching, atomic writes, translation engines, Hugo deployment, etc.) is unified within the common/ package in the root directory.
  • Extension and Workflow: The development workflow engine and all Skills are hosted in the peer independent repository ai-companion (../ai-companion/), integrated into this project via a Hook mechanism.

1. Environment Preparation#

  • Local Translation/Model Environment: Translation and blog functions default to the tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B model running via local Ollama (automatically downloaded upon first use; Linux alternative is vLLM, Windows alternative is transformers).

2. Installation and Initialization#

The project uses editable mode to install the base package and various tool dependencies:

2.1 Install Public Base Package and Most Tool Dependencies#

Install common/ and all tool dependencies except for translator (summarize, research, benchmark, website):

pip install -e ".[all]"

2.2 Install Specific Tool Dependencies#

  • Install Translator independent dependencies (Note: translator is not included in .[all], must be installed separately): 
    pip install -e ".[translator]"
  • Install Website dependencies separately (includes torch + transformers etc. required for local translation): 
    pip install -e ".[website]"

2.3 Run Read-only Smoke Tests#

Verify if all tool environments and imports are normal (does not initiate network requests, LLM calls, or write operations):

bash scripts/smoke.sh

3. Configuration Instructions#

  1. Global Configuration File:
    • Copy the template file from the root directory to generate config.json (this file is gitignored): 
      cp config.example.json config.json
    • Contains running settings for various tools, such as sync (rclone sync configuration) and summarize.
    • The configuration file path can be overridden via the environment variable GADGET_CONFIG.
  2. API Keys and Credentials Directory:
    • The tokens/ directory is used to store API Keys and the new machine initialization list tokens/onboard.yaml (this directory is gitignored, do not commit).
  3. Global Environment Variable Adjustment:
    • GADGET_LLM_BACKEND: Globally specify LLM backends (ollama, claude_cli, anthropic, openai).
    • GADGET_TRANSLATION_BACKEND: Specify translation backends (ollama, llamacpp, vllm, transformers).
    • GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL: Override the default translation model name.

1. Project Summary#

Gadgets is a practical toolkit accumulated by developers in their daily work, designed to automate repetitive tasks in development, research, and content publishing through AI capabilities. It not only contains multiple independent tools but also builds a complete automated workflow through a core shared package (common).

Repository Structure#

  • tools/: Core tools directory, containing five independent tool products. Each tool can run independently.
  • common/: Shared infrastructure package. Provides unified underlying capabilities for all tools, such as LLM calls, JSON parsing, disk caching, atomic writes, translation engines, and Hugo deployment functions.
  • scripts/: Operations and maintenance scripts, used for data synchronization, new machine initialization configuration, etc.
  • outputs/: Storage location for all generated artifacts (reports, cache, logs, data, etc.).
  • docs/: Design documents and archives.
  • ai-companion/ (External Repository): A sibling directory associated via hook, responsible for providing the development workflow engine (planning/execution/change tracking) and all Claude Code related skills.

Tool Functionality Overview#

  1. Summarize: AI conversation summarization tool. Automatically reads AI conversation records from different devices (Claude/ChatGPT, etc.) to generate daily/weekly/monthly reports.
  2. Research: Academic research tool. Supports paper discovery, deep paper insights (analyzing writing structure/OpenReview comments), researcher profile analysis, and citation graph analysis.
  3. Benchmark: Performance testing suite. Cross-platform (NVIDIA/Apple/Intel) CPU/GPU floating-point operation performance testing.
  4. Website: Hugo blog management. Includes automatic media compression, bilingual translation, and automated build and publish processes.
  5. Translator: Document translator. A Gradio-based local translation Web interface that supports translating documents, images, and files while maintaining Markdown format.

2. Usage Tutorial#

This tutorial is intended for users encountering Gadgets for the first time.

I. Environment Preparation#

Before starting, please ensure your system has the following environments installed:

  • Python 3.10+ (It is recommended to use Conda to manage environments, such as conda activate AI)
  • Node.js 18+ (Primarily used for the associated ai-companion repository)
  • Ollama (Recommended, for running LLMs locally)

II. Installation and Configuration#

  1. Install core package and most tools: Enter the project root directory and run the following command to install the common package and dependencies required by most tools:

    pip install -e ".[all]"

  2. Install Translator tool (requires additional installation): Since the translator depends on specific Gradio and model stacks, it must be installed separately:

    pip install -e ".[translator]"

  3. Initialize Configuration:

    • The project uses config.json for configuration. Please first copy one from the template: 
      cp config.example.json config.json
    • One-click configuration for new machines: If you are deploying on a brand new server, you can use the built-in onboarding script (requires preparing tokens/onboard.yaml first): 
      python scripts/onboard.py

III. Typical Tool Usage#

1. Summarize (Conversation Summarization)#

This tool runs through a two-stage workflow: first exporting data, then merging to generate reports.

  • Stage 1: Export unexported dates 
    python -m summarize daily export
  • Stage 2: Sync and merge by day 
    python -m summarize daily merge --sync-all
  • Generate weekly/monthly reports and deploy 
    python -m summarize weekly generate --week 2026-W12 --deploy
python -m summarize monthly generate --month 2026-02 --deploy
  • One-click full process (Export $\rightarrow$ Merge $\rightarrow$ Weekly Report $\rightarrow$ Monthly Report $\rightarrow$ Deploy) 
    python -m summarize auto --deploy
  • Tip: You can switch backends via the --api parameter, such as --api ollama or --api openai.
2. Research (Academic Research)#

Use the unified entry point research_scout.py for operations.

  • Execute full research pipeline (Search $\rightarrow$ Evaluate $\rightarrow$ Report) 
    python tools/research/research_scout.py report --project my-project
  • Search for papers using natural language 
    python tools/research/research_scout.py ask "Find Pieter Abbeel's recent robotics manipulation papers"
  • View researcher profile 
    python tools/research/research_scout.py profile "Sergey Levine"
  • Analyze paper citation graph (using arXiv ID) 
    python tools/research/research_scout.py citations 2301.12597

Note: Please enter the tool directory before running.

cd tools/benchmark

4. Website (Blog Management)#
  • Local preview

Project Summary#

Gadgets is a toolkit designed to simplify daily development workflows. It integrates multiple functional modules such as AI assistants, academic research, performance benchmarking, automated blog publishing, and document translation.

Repository Structure* tools/: The core functional area of the project, containing 5 independent tools:#

*   `summarize`: Processes AI conversation logs to generate daily/weekly/monthly summary reports.
*   `research`: Academic research tool, including paper discovery, researcher analysis, and citation graphs.
*   `benchmark`: A cross-platform CPU/GPU performance benchmarking suite.
*   `website`: A blog system based on Hugo, including automated deployment and media compression.
*   `translator`: A document translation tool based on Gradio, supporting multiple formats while preserving Markdown formatting.
  • common/: Shared infrastructure package, containing common functions such as LLM calls, caching, translation engines, Hugo deployment, etc.
  • scripts/: Operations and maintenance scripts, handling data synchronization, environment initialization, language checks, etc.
  • outputs/: Storage for all generated content (logs, reports, cache, etc.), not counted in the Git repository.
  • ai-companion (Independent Repository): Located in the same-level directory, providing development workflows, code change tracking, and a series of AI skills.

Usage Tutorial#

This tutorial aims to help beginners quickly get started with the Gadget project.

1. Environment Preparation#

Before starting, please ensure your machine meets the following requirements:

  • Python: 3.10+ (recommended to use the Conda environment named AI).
  • Node.js: 18+ (mainly used for the ai-companion module).
  • Basic Dependencies: It is recommended to install the basic rclone tool first (used for data synchronization).

2. Installation and Initialization#

After cloning the repository, enter the project root directory and execute the following steps:

Basic Installation (includes core tools and most functions):

pip install -e ".[all]"

If translation functions are needed (requires additional dependency installation):

pip install -e ".[translator]"

New Machine Initialization (automatic environment configuration): If this is your first time configuring this project on a specific machine, you can use the onboarding script:

  1. Fill in onboard.yaml (containing API Keys and other information) in the tokens/ directory.
  2. Run the following command to complete the configuration automatically (including SSH, tool configuration, rclone initialization, etc.): 
    python scripts/onboard.py

3. Core Tool Usage Guide#

Each tool can be run independently in its corresponding directory or called through a unified module.

A. AI Conversation Summarization (Summarize)#

Used to organize your AI conversation logs (Claude, ChatGPT, etc.) into structured reports.

  • Fully Automated Workflow (Recommended): 
    python -m summarize auto --deploy
  • Step-by-step Operations:
    • Export unexported dates: python -m summarize daily export
    • Merge dates: python -m summarize daily merge --sync-all
    • Generate weekly reports: python -m summarize weekly generate --week 2026-W12 --deploy
    • Generate monthly reports: python -m summarize monthly generate --month 2026-02 --deploy
B. Academic Research (Research)#

Provides paper retrieval, deep analysis, researcher profiling, and citation graph analysis.

  • Start Full Research Workflow: 
    python tools/research/research_scout.py report --project my-project
  • Natural Language Search: 
    python tools/research/research_scout.py ask "Find recent robotics manipulation papers by Pieter Abbeel"
  • Get Researcher Profile: 
    python tools/research/research_scout.py profile "Sergey Levine"
  • Analyze Citation Graph of a Specific Literature: 
    python tools/research/research_scout.py citations 2301.12597
C. Performance Benchmarking (Benchmark)#

Cross-platform CPU/GPU performance testing. Note: Please enter the corresponding directory before execution.

cd tools/benchmark
# 运行所有基准测试并将结果追加到 CSV
python -m benchmark.cli
# 仅测试 GPU
python -m benchmark.cli --gpu-only
# 运行测试并生成 HTML 报告
python -m benchmark.cli --report
# 生成报告并发布到 Hugo 网站
python -m benchmark.cli --report --deploy
D. Document Translation (Translator)#

Starts a Gradio interface for translating various documents (supports .md, .pdf, .docx, etc.).

  • Start Translation Interface: 
    python -m translator
E. Blog Sync and Deployment (Website)#

Used to manage and update the Hugo blog.

  • Install Related Dependencies: pip install -e ".[website]"
  • Update and Push Content:
    • Windows: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/website/update.ps1
    • Linux/macOS: cd tools/website && bash update.sh
  • Local Preview: 
    cd tools/website && hugo server -D

4. Other Common Operations#

  • Data Synchronization: If you operate on multiple devices, you can use the sync scripts: 
    python scripts/sync.py push
# or
python scripts/sync.py pull
  • Switch LLM Backend: All tools supporting LLM (Summarize, Research) can switch backends via the --api parameter: ollama (default), claude_cli, anthropic, openai.
    • Example: python -m summarize auto --api anthropic

5. Notes#

  • Configuration Files: Core project configurations are located in config.json in the root directory (please copy config.example.json for first-time use).
  • Output Directory: All generated content will be saved in the outputs/ folder.
  • Git Norms: Do not commit outputs/, build/, gadget.egg-info, or deployment-related content under tools/website/.

1. Project Summary: What is Gadget?#

Gadget is an open-source developer toolset repository designed to solve daily development pain points through automated scripts and integrated workflows. It is not just a codebase, but a complete ecosystem covering AI report generation, academic research assistance, performance benchmarking, blog automated O&M, and document translation.

The project adopts a “shared infrastructure + independent tools” architectural design. All tools rely on the common package in the root directory to handle common tasks such as LLM calls, caching, and atomic writes.

Repository Structure Overview#

gadget/
├── tools/              # 核心工具目录（每个子目录是一个独立应用）
│   ├── summarize/      # AI 对话日报/周报/月报生成器
│   ├── research/       # 论文发现、研究者分析、引用图谱工具
│   ├── benchmark/      # CPU/GPU 跨平台性能基准测试
│   ├── website/        # 基于 Hugo 的个人博客站点（含自动压缩与部署）
│   └── translator/     # 基于 Gradio 的本地文档翻译 Web 应用
├── common/             # 共享基础设施包（LLM API、缓存、翻译引擎、Hugo 部署）
├── scripts/            # 运维脚本（数据同步、新机器初始化、冒烟测试）
├── docs/               # 设计文档、计划、审计报告
├── outputs/            # 所有生成产物的存放地（已 gitignore，可重建）
├── AGENTS.md           # AI 代理工作协议
├── CLAUDE.md           # Claude Code 指引
└── pyproject.toml      # Python 打包配置（支持 pip install -e .）

Note: Development workflows and Skills are located in the independent same-level repository ../ai-companion/.

Detailed Tool Functions#

Tool Name Core Function Key Features
Summarize AI Conversation Daily/Weekly/Monthly Reports Automatically reads conversation logs from Claude Code/Codex/ChatGPT, etc., and uses LLMs to generate structured reports. Supports multi-device data aggregation and automatic statistics for Token usage and costs.
Research Research Assistant 1. Paper Discovery: Retrieves papers from sources like arXiv/PubMed, generating weekly reports via a three-stage LLM evaluation.
2. Deep Insights: Analyzes paper writing structures and publication strategies, matching OpenReview comments.
3. Researcher Profiling: Analyzes scholar trajectories, calculates scores, and discovers mentor-student relationships.
4. Citation Graph: Performs forward/backward citation analysis based on Semantic Scholar.
Benchmark Performance Benchmarking Cross-platform (CUDA/MPS/XPU) measurement of CPU/GPU floating-point performance. Supports multiple precisions from FP64 to FP8. Results are accumulated in CSV, supporting the generation of Plotly interactive HTML reports and deployment to the blog.
Website Hugo Blog Automation Personal blog site. Core features include incremental media compression (only compressing newly changed images/videos) and bilingual translation. Automatically writes reports and charts generated by the above tools into the blog and deploys them to GitHub Pages.
Translator Local Document Translation Gradio-based Web interface. Supports formats such as .md/.pdf/.docx/images, etc. Uses local models (Ollama/Transformers, etc.) to protect Markdown formatting (code blocks and URLs are not translated).
Common Shared Base Library Provides a unified LLM interface (supporting Ollama/Claude CLI/Anthropic/OpenAI), SHA-256 disk caching, atomic writes, local translation engines, etc.

2. Detailed Gadget Usage Tutorial#

This tutorial is intended for developers using Gadget for the first time. We will proceed in the order of Environment Preparation -> Installation & Configuration -> Tool Usage.

Phase One: Environment Preparation and Installation#

1.1 Environment Requirements#

  • Python: 3.10+ (recommended to use a Conda environment named AI)
  • Node.js: 18+ (only required when using functions from the ai-companion repository)
  • Dependency Tools:
    • rclone: Used for data synchronization (optional, mandatory for multi-device users)
    • Hugo: Static site generator (used for the Website tool)
    • pngquant & HandBrakeCLI: Used for media compression (used for the Website tool, optional but recommended)
    • Ollama: Local LLM runtime environment (recommended, used for default LLM backend and translation)

1.2 Clone Repository#

# 克隆主仓库
git clone git@github.com:TzJ2006/gadget.git
cd gadget

# 克隆 AI 伴侣仓库（同级目录，用于开发工作流和技能）
git clone git@github.com:TzJ2006/ai-companion.git ../ai-companion

1.3 Install Python Dependencies#

Gadget uses pyproject.toml to manage dependencies.Option A: Install all core tool dependencies except Translator (Recommended for most users)

# 激活 Python 环境
conda activate AI  # 或者你的虚拟环境

# 安装 common 包及 summarize, research, benchmark, website 的依赖
pip install -e ".[all]"

Option B: If document translation functionality is required [all] does not include translator because its dependencies are large (involving the GPU inference stack).

# 单独安装 Translator 依赖
pip install -e ".[translator]"

Note: translator dependencies include gradio, gguf translation stack, etc.

1.4 Configure Configuration Files#

Tool configurations are located in config.json at the repository root (this file is gitignored and must be created manually).

  1. Copy the example configuration: 
    cp config.example.json config.json
  2. Edit config.json to fill in necessary API keys (if you use Claude/Anthropic/OpenAI backends) or adjust other settings.
    • LLM 后端切换: Globally controlled via the --api parameter or the GADGET_LLM_BACKEND environment variable.
    • 翻译模型: Uses tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B by default, which is automatically downloaded upon first run.

1.5 One-click Initialization for New Machines (Optional)#

If you are configuring on a new server, you can use the built-in Onboard script to automatically configure SSH, CLI authentication, Pip dependencies, etc.

# 1. 填写 tokens/onboard.yaml (包含 SSH 密钥、API Keys 等敏感信息，请勿提交)
# 2. 运行初始化脚本
python scripts/onboard.py

This script will automatically complete: SSH configuration, Claude/Codex CLI installation and authentication, Pip Extras installation, and Rclone basic configuration.

Phase Two: Typical Usage of Each Tool#

2.1 Summarize: AI Conversation Daily/Weekly/Monthly Reports#

This tool automatically aggregates your AI conversation logs from different devices (Claude Code, Codex, ChatGPT, etc.) to generate statistical reports.

Prerequisites: Ensure the log export function of each AI tool is enabled, or manually export logs to the specified directory.

Typical Workflow:

  1. Phase 1: Export Conversation Logs Extract conversation logs for all unexported dates.

    python -m summarize daily export

  2. Phase 2: Sync and Merge If you have multiple devices, first sync data via scripts/sync.py, then merge daily data.

    # Sync data for all dates and merge them day by day
python -m summarize daily merge --sync-all

  3. Generate Reports

    # Generate a weekly report for a specified week and deploy to the blog
python -m summarize weekly generate --week 2026-W12 --deploy

# Generate a monthly report for a specified month and deploy to the blog
python -m summarize monthly generate --month 2026-02 --deploy

  4. One-click Full Process (Recommended) Automatically executes: Export -> Merge -> Generate Weekly Report -> Generate Monthly Report -> Deploy.

    python -m summarize auto --deploy

Tip: Uses ollama backend (local Qwen3.8-27B) by default, no API Key required. To switch, use --api claude_cli or --api anthropic.

2.2 Research: Research Assistant#

This is a powerful academic tool that supports natural language queries, deep paper analysis, scholar profiling, and citation mapping.

1. Natural Language Paper Search Automatically routes to appropriate data sources (arXiv, PubMed, etc.).

python tools/research/research_scout.py ask "找 Pieter Abbeel 最近的机器人操作论文"

2. Generate Complete Research Weekly Reports Executes the full process: Search -> Three-stage LLM evaluation (Fast Screening -> Deep Evaluation -> Citation Impact) -> Report Generation.

python tools/research/research_scout.py report --project my-project

3. Researcher Profiling Obtain a scholar’s papers and citation data to generate trajectory analysis, scores, and mentor-student relationships.

python tools/research/research_scout.py profile "Sergey Levine"

4. Citation Map Analysis Based on arXiv ID or DOI, analyze forward citations and backward references.

python tools/research/research_scout.py citations 2301.12597

5. Deploy Reports to Blog

python tools/research/research_scout.py deploy

2.3 Benchmark: Performance Benchmarking#

Measures CPU/GPU FLOPS performance, supporting NVIDIA (CUDA), Apple Silicon (MPS), and Intel (XPU).

Note: The Benchmark command must be executed in the tools/benchmark/ directory.

1. Run All Benchmarks Results will be appended to a CSV file (supports multi-hardware accumulation).

cd tools/benchmark
python -m benchmark.cli

2. Test CPU or GPU Only

python -m benchmark.cli --cpu-only
python -m benchmark.cli --gpu-only

3. Generate HTML Report

python -m benchmark.cli --report

4. Generate Report and Deploy to Blog Publish benchmark results to the /benchmark/ path of the Hugo website.

python -m benchmark.cli --report --deploy

View report: Visit https://tzj2006.github.io/benchmark/

2.4 Website: Hugo Blog Automation#

This tool is responsible for integrating content generated by other tools (daily reports, weekly reports, charts) into the blog, and handling media compression and bilingual translation.

1. Update Blog (Compress + Build + Deploy) This is the core command; it performs incremental compression (processing only new files), Hugo build, and pushes to GitHub Pages.

# macOS / Linux
cd tools/website && bash update.sh

# Windows
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/website/update.ps1

2. Local Preview Start the Hugo development server locally to view drafts and recent changes.

cd tools/website
hugo server -D

Note: -D indicates including Drafts.

3. Translation Mechanism The Website tool has a built-in translation engine. During the build process, it automatically detects bilingual content and calls local models (default tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B) for translation.

  • Default backend: ollama
  • Alternative backends: vllm (Linux), transformers (Windows)
  • Models are downloaded automatically, no manual configuration required.

2.5 Translator: Local Document Translation#

Provides a Web interface for translating local files (.md, .pdf, .docx, images, etc.) while preserving Markdown formatting.

1. Start Translation Service

# 确保已安装 translator 依赖: pip install -e ".[translator]"
python -m translator

After starting, the Gradio interface will automatically open in your browser.

2. How to Use

  1. Open the local address in your browser (usually http://127.0.0.1:7860).
  2. Upload a file or input text.
  3. Select source and target languages (supports auto auto-detection).
  4. Click translate.
  5. Copy the result or download the translated file.

Advanced Configuration:

  • Model Switching: Uses tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B by default. You can switch via the model management interface in the GUI or by setting the GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL environment variable.
  • Backend Switching: Prioritizes ollama by default. If Ollama is not installed, it will automatically fall back to transformers (Windows) or vllm (Linux). You can also force specify via GADGET_TRANSLATION_BACKEND.

Phase Three: Operations and Data Synchronization#

3.1 Data Synchronization (Rclone)#

If you are developing across multiple devices, you can use the built-in sync scripts.

# 查看同步状态
python scripts/sync.py status

# 推送本地更改到云端
python scripts/sync.py push

# 从云端拉取最新数据
python scripts/sync.py pull

Configuration is located in the sync section of config.json.

3.2 Smoke Test#

Before running the full process, you can quickly check if the environment is configured correctly (read-only operation, does not consume LLM Tokens).

bash scripts/smoke.sh

3.3 Output Directory Management#

All generated items (logs, reports, charts, cache) are stored in the outputs/ directory.

  • This directory is ignored by .gitignore.
  • If outputs/ is deleted, all reports can be rebuilt by re-running the corresponding generate command of the respective tool.

FAQ#

Q: How do I use different LLM backends? A: Most tools support the --api parameter.

  • ollama (Default): Runs locally, no Key required, Qwen3.8-27B recommended.
  • claude_cli: Reuses the login status of Claude Code, no additional API Key required.
  • anthropic: Uses Anthropic API Key.
  • openai: Uses OpenAI API Key. The global default value can be set via the GADGET_LLM_BACKEND environment variable.

Q: Why is translation so slow or failing? A: Translation uses local inference.

  1. Ensure Ollama is running and the model has been pulled (ollama pull tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B).
  2. If Ollama is not available, the program will fall back to transformers (high CPU/memory consumption) or vllm (GPU).
  3. Check if the GADGET_TRANSLATION_BACKEND environment variable correctly points to your installed backend.

Q: Blog deployment failed? A:

  1. Check the Hugo path and Git configuration in config.json.
  2. Ensure the tools/website/public/ directory is a separate Git repository (usually managed automatically by scripts; do not manually git add files under this directory to the main repository).
  3. Check the build logs in outputs/logs/.

Q: How do I back up? A: Your source code is in Git. For your data (conversation logs, CSV benchmark data, generated reports), it is recommended to keep them outside the outputs/ directory or sync them to the cloud via scripts/sync.py. The tokens/ directory contains sensitive information; please back it up yourself and do not commit it to Git.

End of tutorial. Happy using! If you have more questions, please refer to TUTORIAL.md and the documentation in each tool’s directory.

    Uses `tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B` by default; it will be downloaded automatically on the first run.
    Can be overridden via the `GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL` environment variable.

3.  **Backend switching**
    Ollama is prioritized by default. Falls back to transformers on Windows; vLLm or GGUF can be configured on Linux.

### 4. Operations and Maintenance (Scripts)

#### Data Sync (Sync)
Used for synchronizing data generated by summarize/website/research, etc., across multiple devices.
```bash
# 推送数据
python scripts/sync.py push

# 拉取数据
python scripts/sync.py pull

# 查看状态
python scripts/sync.py status

Configured in the sync section of config.json. rclone must be configured first.

Onboarding (New Machine Quick Setup)#

If it is a new machine, fill in tokens/onboard.yaml and run:

python scripts/onboard.py

This will automatically complete SSH, CLI authentication, pip dependency installation, and rclone bootstrap.

One-click Server-level Deployment#

System-level installation (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) for Ubuntu servers is located in the ai-companion repository:

bash ../ai-companion/scripts/onboard-server.sh --help
# 示例用法 (需传入 ai-companion 路径)
# bash ../ai-companion/scripts/onboard-server.sh --companion-repo git@github.com:TzJ2006/ai-companion.git

5. Output and Notes#

  • All generated files are located in the outputs/ directory (logs, reports, cache, etc.), which has been added to .gitignore.
  • Do not commit:
    • Any content under outputs/.
    • Keys under tokens/.
    • tools/website/public/ (it is a standalone repository).
    • build/ and gadget.egg-info/.
    • Data synchronized by rclone.
  • LLM Backend Switching: Can be set globally via the GADGET_LLM_BACKEND environment variable, or by using the --api parameter in various tool commands.

By following the steps above, you can fully run all core tools in the Gadget project. For detailed advanced configurations (such as specific tool JSON formats or more CLI parameters), please refer to TUTORIAL.md or README.md under each tool’s directory.

Reproducing#

docbench.py (run, resumable) → docbench.json (full record) → gen_doc_post.py (builds this page).
